+# Finite record bounds and the entire opposite half-line
+
+## Abstract
+
+Finite record bounds and the entire opposite half-line
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The exact finite erased observation field).**
+
+$$\forall k:(Nat), (\forall n:(Nat), (\operatorname{recordField}(k, n)= \operatorname{generatedField}((z:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{pair}(\operatorname{leftWord}(k, z), \operatorname{rightWord}(n, z))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleHalfLines.recordField` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For natural k and n, recordField(k,n) is the sigma-field on the original visible integer-time path generated by the chronological words X[-k,-1] and X[1,n]. The erased coordinate X0 is absent, and either observed word may be empty.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Two ordered limits preserve the same finite bound).**
+
+$$\forall P:(\operatorname{Measure}(Int\to Bool)), ([\operatorname{IsProbabilityMeasure}(P)]\forall Y:((Int\to Bool)\to Real), (\forall j:(Nat), (\forall BL:((Int\to Bool)\to Real), (\forall BR:((Int\to Bool)\to Real), ((\forall k:(Nat), (\forall n:(Nat), ((j\le k)\implies (\operatorname{AE}(P, (z:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{abs}((\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{recordField}(k, n), z))-(\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{recordField}(j, n), z)))\le \operatorname{apply}(BL, z)))))))\implies ((\forall k:(Nat), (\forall n:(Nat), ((j\le n)\implies (\operatorname{AE}(P, (z:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{abs}((\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{recordField}(k, n), z))-(\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{recordField}(k, j), z)))\le \operatorname{apply}(BR, z)))))))\implies (\operatorname{AE}(P, (z:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{abs}((\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{generatedField}(exterior), z))-(\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{generatedField}(\operatorname{leftObservation}(j)), z)))\le \operatorname{apply}(BL, z)))\land (\operatorname{AE}(P, (z:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{abs}((\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{generatedField}(exterior), z))-(\operatorname{condExp}(P, Y, \operatorname{generatedField}(\operatorname{rightObservation}(j)), z)))\le \operatorname{apply}(BR, z)))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleHalfLines.finite_record_bounds_to_half_lines` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Fix any one probability measure P on the original visible integer-time path space, real-valued function Y, natural retained length j and real-valued bounds B_L and B_R. Suppose for every k,n with k>=j the absolute difference between the P conditional expectations of Y given recordField(k,n) and recordField(j,n) is at most B_L almost everywhere. Suppose also that for every k,n with n>=j the corresponding difference for recordField(k,n) and recordField(k,j) is at most B_R. Then the full exterior conditional expectation differs from the conditional expectation given (leftWord(j),after) by at most B_L almost everywhere, and from that given (before,rightWord(j)) by at most B_R almost everywhere. Here before and after are the entire infinite visible half-lines, and exterior is their pair. Both conclusions use the original P and exactly the original bound functions. The left argument first completes k and then n. The right argument first completes n and then k. Each passage uses almost-sure upward conditional-expectation convergence and closedness of the scalar inequality, on a common countable intersection of full-measure events. No L2 convergence claim is needed.
+
+In the formulas, generatedField(f) means MeasurableSpace.comap(f) with the canonical product measurable space on the observation type. condExp(P,Y,m,z) is the value at z of the P conditional expectation of Y given m, and AE(P,(z maps to p)) means p holds P-almost everywhere. Int, Nat, Bool and Real denote the corresponding Lean types.
+
+The finite fields split into the join of the left-word and right-word fields. The supremum of the chronological left-word fields is exactly the before field, and the supremum of the right-word fields is exactly the after field: each finite word is a measurable function of its half-line, while every half-line coordinate occurs in some finite word. Taking these joins proves all four supremum identities used by the two ordered limits. Thus no retained infinite half-line is replaced by a finite window at the last step, including j=0.
+
+In rectangle smoothing, take Y=erasedBit and P to be the visible pushforward of the one native class-restricted original joint law. The intended bounds are rho raised to the left and right original visible success counts. The finite_record_smoothing_by_original_success_count supplier provides bounds for its finite recordPosterior ratios on positive records. Identifying those ratios with these conditional expectations, discarding zero record fibers only on their null sets, and matching the two count conventions are the finite adapters needed before the present limit theorem applies. The chronological_success_moment estimate then controls the squared count under the same original law. Squaring and integrating the resulting posterior bounds and summing the quotient groups gives the separate squared-defect and root-tail conclusions.
+

+# Chronological rectangle occurrence moments
+
+## Abstract
+
+Chronological rectangle occurrence moments
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The complete original marked past at a cut).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), ([\operatorname{MeasurableSpace}(H)]\forall t:(Int), (\operatorname{markedField}(t)= \operatorname{generatedField}((z:\operatorname{PathSpace}(H)\mapsto \operatorname{pair}(\operatorname{state}(t, z), \operatorname{past}(t, z))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleMoments.markedField` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For any measurable hidden type H and integer t, markedField(t) is the sigma-field generated by the pair consisting of H(t) and the entire sequence of hidden states and emitted bits strictly before t. It contains every hidden coordinate through t and every output coordinate below t. It contains no output at t or later.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (One success depends only on the block's emitted bits).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), (\forall w:(\operatorname{List}(Bool)), (\forall b:(Nat), (\forall d:(Int), (\operatorname{blockSuccess}(H, w, b, d)= \operatorname{preimage}(\operatorname{future}(H, d), \operatorname{success}(w, b))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleMoments.blockSuccess` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+blockSuccess(w,b,d) is the original event that w is an infix of the b consecutive emitted bits beginning at integer d. It is the preimage of OriginalRectangleOccurrence.success(w,b) under the original future(d) map. Hidden starting states do not enter this event.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The original chronological block count).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), (\forall w:(\operatorname{List}(Bool)), (\forall b:(Nat), (\forall d:(Int), (\forall q:(Nat), (\forall z:(\operatorname{PathSpace}(H)), (\operatorname{chronologicalCount}(w, b, d, q, z)= \operatorname{sumRange}(q, (i:Nat\mapsto \operatorname{ite}(z\in \operatorname{blockSuccess}(w, b, (d)+((\operatorname{intCast}(i))\cdot (\operatorname{intCast}(b)))), 1, 0)))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleMoments.chronologicalCount` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+chronologicalCount(w,b,d,q) is the sum of the success indicators for the q disjoint blocks beginning at d, d+b, through d+(q-1)b, in that time order. Each block pays once, regardless of how many occurrences lie inside it. An empty block sequence has count zero.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (The same-law conditional success probability).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), ([\operatorname{Fintype}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSpace}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSingletonClass}(H)]\forall theta:(\operatorname{Presentation}(H)), (\forall J:(\operatorname{Measure}(\operatorname{PathSpace}(H))), ([\operatorname{IsProbabilityMeasure}(J)](\operatorname{HasOriginalCylinders}(J, theta))\implies (\forall w:(\operatorname{List}(Bool)), (\forall R:(\operatorname{Rectangle}(\operatorname{product}(theta, w))), (\forall r:(H), ((r\in \operatorname{rows}(R))\implies (\forall a:(\forall h:(H), (\operatorname{LabelledRoute}(theta, h, r))), ((\forall h:(H), (\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{apply}(a, h))\le \operatorname{card}(H)))\implies (\forall t:(Int), (\operatorname{AE}(J, (z:\operatorname{PathSpace}(H)\mapsto \operatorname{selectedEpsilon}(theta, w, r, a)\le \operatorname{condExp}(J, \operatorname{indicator}(\operatorname{blockSuccess}(w, (\operatorname{length}(w))+(\operatorname{card}(H)), t), \operatorname{constFunction}(\operatorname{PathSpace}(H), 1)), \operatorname{markedField}(t), z))))))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleMoments.marked_success_condExp` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let theta be any original stationary binary edge presentation on finite measurable H, and J any probability measure with theta's original marked cylinders. Fix a Boolean word w, a support rectangle for product(theta,w), a row r in its row support, and the given family a of positive labelled original routes from every h to r, each of length at most card(H). Set b=length(w)+card(H), and keep exactly the selectedEpsilon(theta,w,r,a) of that family. For every integer t, the conditional expectation under J of the blockSuccess(w,b,t) indicator given markedField(t) is at least this epsilon almost everywhere. The complete marked-past occurrence inequality is summed over the finite hidden fibers for an arbitrary measurable event of markedField(t). Its real integral characterization then gives the conditional-expectation lower bound. Null hidden fibers remain in the sum and require no division.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Successes pay the squared contraction in chronological time).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), ([\operatorname{Fintype}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSpace}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSingletonClass}(H)]\forall theta:(\operatorname{Presentation}(H)), (\forall J:(\operatorname{Measure}(\operatorname{PathSpace}(H))), ([\operatorname{IsProbabilityMeasure}(J)](\operatorname{HasOriginalCylinders}(J, theta))\implies (\forall w:(\operatorname{List}(Bool)), (\forall R:(\operatorname{Rectangle}(\operatorname{product}(theta, w))), (\forall r:(H), ((r\in \operatorname{rows}(R))\implies (\forall a:(\forall h:(H), (\operatorname{LabelledRoute}(theta, h, r))), ((\forall h:(H), (\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{apply}(a, h))\le \operatorname{card}(H)))\implies (\forall rho:(Real), ((0\le rho)\implies ((rho\le 1)\implies (\forall d:(Int), (\forall q:(Nat), (let b:=(\operatorname{length}(w))+(\operatorname{card}(H)); let eta:=(1)-((\operatorname{selectedEpsilon}(theta, w, r, a))\cdot ((1)-((rho)^{2}))); \operatorname{integral}(J, (z:\operatorname{PathSpace}(H)\mapsto (rho)^{(2)\cdot (\operatorname{chronologicalCount}(w, b, d, q, z))}))\le (eta)^{q})))))))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleMoments.chronological_success_moment` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Under the same presentation, same original-cylinder probability J, same word, rectangle, support row and given route family as above, take any real rho with 0<=rho<=1, any integer start d and natural block count q. Let b=length(w)+card(H), epsilon=selectedEpsilon(theta,w,r,a), eta=1-epsilon*(1-rho^2), and K=chronologicalCount(w,b,d,q). The J integral of rho^(2*K) is at most eta^q. The single-block factor is rho^2 on success and one otherwise. Its conditional expectation at the block start is at most eta by the preceding conditional probability bound. All earlier factors are measurable in the complete marked past at the next block start; pulling them out and taking total expectation gives one factor eta at each step. No independence, future-conditioned success estimate, positivity of every matrix entry, aperiodicity or unifilarity is imposed. The case q=0 is the integral of one, including rho=0; eta may also be zero.
+
+The blockSuccess defining equality displays its implicit hidden type H explicitly in blockSuccess(H,w,b,d) and future(H,d). In the formulas, generatedField(f) means the comap of the canonical product measurable space along f; condExp(J,f,m,z) is the conditional expectation of f given m evaluated at z. sumRange(q,f) is the natural finite sum over i in Finset.range(q); indicator(S,f), constFunction(T,c), preimage, integral and intCast have their corresponding Lean meanings. AE(J,(z maps to p)) denotes the almost-everywhere quantifier under J.
+
+For a native source component C, instantiate theta with nativeComponent and use the very original-cylinder law on C identified by component_restriction. Choose the routes furnished by OriginalRectangleRoutes, without changing the selected family or its epsilon. Put rho=1-u/v from the original support rectangle. For q=floor(j/b), the left count uses d=-q*b and the right count uses d=1. These are respectively the source blocks [-q*b+(i-1)b,-q*b+i*b-1] and [1+(i-1)b,i*b], for i from one through q. Both applications average in chronological original time under this one class-restricted measure, even though the finite right-posterior comparison propagates in reverse. At j=0 both block counts are empty. The identity with the finite-list count in finite_record_smoothing_by_original_success_count and the identification of finite-record posteriors with conditional expectations supply the separate connections from posterior differences to these moments.
+

+# Original rectangle posteriors and squared erasure defects
+
+## Abstract
+
+Original rectangle posteriors and squared erasure defects
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The support rectangle gives a contraction parameter below one).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), ([\operatorname{Fintype}(H)]\forall B:(\operatorname{Matrix}(H, H, Real)), (\forall R:(\operatorname{Rectangle}(B)), (0\le (1)-(\frac{\operatorname{rectangleMinimum}(B, R)}{\operatorname{rectangleMaximum}(B, R)})\land ((1)-(\frac{\operatorname{rectangleMinimum}(B, R)}{\operatorname{rectangleMaximum}(B, R)})< 1))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectanglePosteriors.rectangle_rho_range` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every real matrix B on a finite index type and every positive support rectangle R, OriginalRectangleSmoothing.extrema supplies 0 < u <= v for its least and greatest rectangle entries. Hence rho=1-u/v lies in [0,1), including rho=0. The same statement supplies the range in the posterior proof and the native component theorem.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (The finite ratios and chronological counts meet on the same original law).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), ([\operatorname{Fintype}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSpace}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSingletonClass}(H)]\forall theta:(\operatorname{Presentation}(H)), (\forall J:(\operatorname{Measure}(\operatorname{PathSpace}(H))), ([\operatorname{IsProbabilityMeasure}(J)](\operatorname{HasOriginalCylinders}(J, theta))\implies (\forall w:(\operatorname{List}(Bool)), ((w\neq \operatorname{nil}())\implies (\forall R:(\operatorname{Rectangle}(\operatorname{product}(theta, w))), (\forall r:(H), ((r\in \operatorname{rows}(R))\implies (\forall a:(\forall h:(H), (\operatorname{LabelledRoute}(theta, h, r))), ((\forall h:(H), (\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{apply}(a, h))\le \operatorname{card}(H)))\implies (\forall j:(Nat), (let P:=\operatorname{map}(J, snd); let b:=(\operatorname{length}(w))+(\operatorname{card}(H)); let rho:=(1)-(\frac{\operatorname{rectangleMinimum}(\operatorname{product}(theta, w), R)}{\operatorname{rectangleMaximum}(\operatorname{product}(theta, w), R)}); let eta:=(1)-((\operatorname{selectedEpsilon}(theta, w, r, a))\cdot ((1)-((rho)^{2}))); let q:=\operatorname{natDiv}(j, b); \operatorname{AE}(J, (z:\operatorname{PathSpace}(H)\mapsto \operatorname{abs}((\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), exterior, \operatorname{apply}(exterior, \operatorname{snd}(z))))-(\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), \operatorname{leftObservation}(j), \operatorname{apply}(\operatorname{leftObservation}(j), \operatorname{snd}(z)))))\le (rho)^{\operatorname{chronologicalCount}(w, b, (-\operatorname{intCast}(q))\cdot (\operatorname{intCast}(b)), q, z)}\land (\operatorname{abs}((\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), exterior, \operatorname{apply}(exterior, \operatorname{snd}(z))))-(\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), \operatorname{rightObservation}(j), \operatorname{apply}(\operatorname{rightObservation}(j), \operatorname{snd}(z)))))\le (rho)^{\operatorname{chronologicalCount}(w, b, 1, q, z)})))\land (\operatorname{integral}(P, (z:Int\to Bool\mapsto ((\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), exterior, \operatorname{apply}(exterior, z)))-(\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), \operatorname{leftObservation}(j), \operatorname{apply}(\operatorname{leftObservation}(j), z))))^{2}))\le (eta)^{q})\land (\operatorname{integral}(P, (z:Int\to Bool\mapsto ((\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), exterior, \operatorname{apply}(exterior, z)))-(\operatorname{bitPredictor}(P, (x:Int\to Bool\mapsto \operatorname{apply}(x, 0)), \operatorname{rightObservation}(j), \operatorname{apply}(\operatorname{rightObservation}(j), z))))^{2}))\le (eta)^{q})))))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectanglePosteriors.original_rectangle_erasure_bounds` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let H be any finite measurable hidden type with measurable singletons, theta an original stationary binary edge presentation, and J any probability measure on the original marked integer-time path space with HasOriginalCylinders(J,theta). Fix a nonempty Boolean word w, a support rectangle R for product(theta,w), a state r in its row support, and a family a(h) of positive labelled original routes from every hidden h to r, each of length at most card(H). Let j be any natural number. No hypothesis asserts a posterior bound, independence, future-conditioned occurrence, unifilarity, aperiodicity, or positivity outside the support rectangle.
+
+Define P=J.map(Prod.snd), b=length(w)+card(H), u=rectangleMinimum(product(theta,w),R), v=rectangleMaximum(product(theta,w),R), rho=1-u/v, epsilon=selectedEpsilon(theta,w,r,a), eta=1-epsilon*(1-rho^2), and q=j/b. Define q0, pL, and pR to be the total bounded OriginalErasureComparison.bitPredictor versions for the center bit under P, evaluated respectively on exterior=(before,after), leftObservation(j)=(leftWord(j),after), and rightObservation(j)=(before,rightWord(j)). bitPredictor_condExp identifies these versions almost everywhere with the corresponding P conditional expectations of erasedBit. Both before and after are the entire infinite half-lines. The theorem first asserts that, for J-almost every original marked path z, abs(q0(z.2)-pL(z.2)) is at most rho raised to chronologicalCount(w,b,-q*b,q,z), and abs(q0(z.2)-pR(z.2)) is at most rho raised to chronologicalCount(w,b,1,q,z). It then asserts that the P integral of (q0-pL)^2 and the P integral of (q0-pR)^2 are each at most eta^q. All three conclusions retain the same J and its exact visible pushforward P.
+
+In the displayed formulas, integral(P,f) is the real integral of f under P; map, snd and intCast are the measure pushforward, second projection and canonical integer cast. natDiv is natural division, and AE(J,(z maps to p)) means p holds J-almost everywhere. All predictors use the same P and the center-bit map x maps to x(0).
+
+The finite observation is the pair of chronological original words X[-k,-1] and X[1,n]. Its fiber at (a,c) is exactly OriginalRectangleSmoothing.record(List.ofFn(a),List.ofFn(c)). The alphabet is finite, so the union of zero-mass observation fibers is null, including when either word is empty. On every remaining fiber, Mathlib condDistrib_apply_of_ne_zero identifies the conditional distribution with the ratio of the center-true record mass to the full record mass. OriginalErasureComparison.bitPredictor_condExp identifies this ratio with the erasedBit conditional expectation given OriginalRectangleHalfLines.recordField(k,n). There is no division on a null record or hidden fiber.
+
+For k>=j, the chronological left word splits as its earlier prefix followed by the retained j-bit suffix. For n>=j, the chronological right word splits as the retained j-bit prefix followed by the extra future. Those two decompositions are passed directly to finite_record_smoothing_by_original_success_count, using the positive long and short observed records. No reverse or extra-past kernel, transfer contraction, or likelihood matrix bound is reconstructed.
+
+The recursive finite-list success count is identified by induction with the sum of the same visible block-success indicators in chronological order. In a sampled word of length n, each take(b) is the original b-bit block at the current integer start and each drop(b) advances that start by b. The trimmed left word has length (j/b)*b and begins at -j+(j mod b)=-(j/b)*b. The right word begins at 1; its final incomplete block is unused by the count. Thus for i from one through q the left blocks are [-q*b+(i-1)*b,-q*b+i*b-1] and the right blocks are [1+(i-1)*b,i*b]. Every success is a complete w-infix in that block's emitted bits, counted once. None includes X0.
+
+finite_record_bounds_to_half_lines consumes the two finite conditional-expectation inequalities. It completes the past and then the future for left erasure, and the future and then the past for right erasure, without changing either count. Pullback by Prod.snd and the bitPredictor_condExp identities give the two bounds for the actual total bitPredictor versions under J. Squaring, changing variables between P and J, and applying chronological_success_moment at starts -q*b and 1 gives both squared-defect bounds with the original selected epsilon. For the chronological-power integrand, OriginalRectangleMoments.payment_integrable supplies integrability of the chronological product, and payment_power identifies it pointwise with rho^(2*chronologicalCount) under the same measure and parameters. Earlier blocks are paid in forward chronological time on each side; no lower bound after conditioning on a future is used. Integrability is obtained from bounded erasedBit and the conditional-expectation MemLp theorem, not from a claim that Mathlib's L1 martingale limit is an L2 theorem.
+
+At j=0 the two counts are empty and the bound is one, while each observation retains the full opposite infinite half-line. Natural powers preserve rho=0 and 0^0=1. No step divides by rho or eta, so eta=0 is retained. Structural zeros remain governed by the existing positive-record supplier. This source is a reusable probability bridge for a supplied original-cylinder law and original route family. The native-component theorem instantiates theta and J with nativeComponent and the exact class-restricted original law via component_restriction; choose the original routes with irreducible_rectangle_occurrence; identify P with the exact visible law used by the native-component risk definitions; and use tail_series with eta and sqrt(eta) to give both original tails. OriginalRectangleTheorem42 states those native-component and tail conclusions.

+# Original rectangle theorem 4.2 native component consumer
+
+## Abstract
+
+Original rectangle theorem 4.2 native component consumer
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The actual sum of square roots of the two erasure risks).**
+
+$$\forall H:(Type), ([\operatorname{Fintype}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSpace}(H)][\operatorname{MeasurableSingletonClass}(H)]\forall theta:(\operatorname{Presentation}(H)), (\forall R:(Nat), (\operatorname{rootErasureTail}(theta, R)= \operatorname{tsum}((n:Nat\mapsto (\operatorname{sqrt}(\operatorname{leftRisk}(theta, (R)+(n))))+(\operatorname{sqrt}(\operatorname{rightRisk}(theta, (R)+(n)))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/TrajectoryLaws/Rectangles/OriginalRectangleTheorem42.rootErasureTail` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The sum is the real tsum of the square roots of the existing leftRisk and rightRisk. The theorem below separately proves summability of this exact series for every natural lower radius.
+
